title: WHC - Campus West CRM Ticketing System - AWARD
description:
Campus West is a unique entertainment and leisure facility in Welwyn Garden City, owned and managed by Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council (the Council). It offers a three-screen independent cinema which accounts for the venue's bulk of its income - with the Event Cinema offering contributing a significant proportion. The screens also double as spaces for private hire and conferencing activities, while its largest space is a flexible cinema/theatre which every year play host to its hugely popular in-house produced panto. Campus West also houses a soft play centre as well as the only purpose-built roller-skating rink in Hertfordshire. This multi-purpose space, well known as Roller City, is used weekly for Keep Fit, Line Dancing and Zumba classes. To complete this rich mix of diverse and fun filled activities and services, the venue runs a café which caters and provides food and beverage for all ages.
      
      50 years after it opened its doors, pre-pandemic, it sold more than £2.4 million tickets to half a million visitors annually. Campus West which is Council-owned and operated, but functions as a commercial organisation, has nurtured an active Zebra discount membership scheme with over 14,000 members actively engaging in its services. Marketing mailouts promoting Campus West and its upcoming activities are sent weekly to about 37,000 customers who have agreed to receive such emails. And with a Net Promoter Score south of 90, over 80% of Campus West users continue to affirm that this unique venue is value for money. 
      
      Along with Campus West, our present Ticketing CRM solution is deployed in two sister venues: The Watermill at Mill Green Museum and The Hive. Under one single database system with separate and restricted setup, the system is used for day-to-day ticketing, merchandise and food and beverage operations across the board.
      The Council is seeking a suitably experienced supplier to provide a ticketing CRM solution.

title: WHC - Electrical pool cars. - AWARD
description:
Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council (hereinafter referred to as the Council) is seeking to procure under the Crown Commercial Services Framework Agreement Code RM6265, titled: Vehicle Hire Solution (Lot 5 - Car Share Solution) an electric pool car scheme for its employees and members of the public, with the aim of reducing carbon footprint and mileage travelled in 'grey fleet' vehicles too.
      
      A number of Council employees are signed up to the existing scheme, with access to two vehicles. The scheme is also available to members of the public at designated times outside of the council's contracted hours as a 'car club' scheme. Members of the public will sign up for the scheme directly with the Service provider. 
      
      The current contract ends 4 June 2026 and the Council is considering for the scheme to continue to operate under current provisions, as detailed in this document.
      
      The vehicles provided should be fully electric vehicles (EVs). The vehicles shall be fully allocated for staff use during working hours and for public use outside of these hours. Both vehicles are totally allocated to public use outside of working hours. However, employees may also join as public members so that they may use the cars out of contract hours as well but will do at preferential rates.
      
      The pricing includes supply of 2 vehicles to Campus East Cherry Tree car park on 5 June 2026.

title: WHC - Local Plan Viability Assessment - AWARD
description:
Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council (hereafter "the Council") wishes to commission a viability assessment for their Local Plan Review. The purpose of this review is to assess the economic viability and feasibility of a revised Local Plan, and to inform policy requirements.
      
      The objective of the required assessment is to determine that the cumulative costs of policies, site requirements and the accompanying package of necessary infrastructure will not undermine the overall deliverability of the Local Plan. The assessment should be robust enough to support the Local Plan Review as part of the evidence base and be relied upon by developers when submitting subsequent planning applications on allocated Local Plan sites.
      
      Whilst not part of this commission, consultants should also be prepared to give evidence at Local Plan Examination, provide expert advice on specific planning applications and to provide expert witness services at planning appeals, as required by the Council. Index linked hourly rates for undertaking such work should be included as part of the tender response.  
      
      It is anticipated that the contract will commence on 11th August 2025 and continue until stage 1 services are completed.

title: Provision of Support and Accommodation for Adults Experiencing Homelessness and Multiple Disadvantage - Welwyn Hatfield 1
description:
This is an Award Notice for the Provision of Support and Accommodation for Adults Experiencing Homelessness and Multiple Disadvantage - Welwyn Hatfield 1. This is a direct award because competition is absent for technical reasons. 

The Service will be free at the point of use and will support single adults aged 18 and over experiencing homelessness and multiple disadvantage in Stevenage. The provider will make available 30 Units of support combination of accommodation based support and floating support as needed to be used flexibly.
 
Services will be focussed to target support to the following groups 
•	High/complex/multiple needs: i.e. Long-term rough sleepers or people encountering repeat homelessness and requiring intensive support through Housing First or supported housing with high-level of management and support. 

•	Medium/high needs: people with fluctuating levels of support, who are experiencing homelessness/rough sleeping and/or who have health, care and support needs best met through a housing-led placement with sufficient support. 

This Service will deliver a strengths based and trauma informed approach to support. The keyworker will listen to and understand the person's priorities, focussing on their personal goals and how they can be supported to live a full, healthy, active, and independent life.
cpvDescriptionExpanded: Health and social work services
